## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `refresh_fingerprints` overwrites the stored fingerprint of a tracked file that was edited by hand. This removes the tamper detection that the pull-request description gives as the reason the existing fingerprints are kept.

## Changes
The pull request adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`, which rewrite the JSON integrity manifest for the names they are given. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py`, which covers both helpers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Keep existing fingerprints in refresh_fingerprints — If you call `refresh_fingerprints` with a tracked name whose file was hand-edited, `entries[name] = fingerprint(root / name)` replaces the original digest with the edited one, so `verify` then passes. The description says "Existing fingerprints let verification detect hand-edited tracked files," and `register_new_files` keeps those fingerprints, but this function does not. The added refresh test only passes an unchanged `tracked.txt`, so it cannot catch this. — Running the refresh command over all files after adding new ones silently accepts any tampered tracked file. — Fix: Either skip names already in `entries`, as `register_new_files` does at `app/integrity.py:24`, or document that refresh re-accepts current content, and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` with an edited tracked file.
